doi-10-18653-v1-2022-acl-long-297.title: LexGLUE: A Benchmark Dataset for Legal Language Understanding in English
doi-10-18653-v1-2022-acl-long-297.support_excerpt: We introduce LexGLUE, a benchmark dataset to evaluate the performance of NLP methods in legal tasks.
doi-10-18653-v1-2022-acl-long-297.claim: LexGLUE establishes standardized benchmark evaluation for legal NLP and domain-specific language understanding.

doi-10-18653-v1-2024-eacl-demo-16.title: RAGAs: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
doi-10-18653-v1-2024-eacl-demo-16.support_excerpt: We present Ragas, a framework for reference-free evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems across faithfulness, answer relevance, and context recall.
doi-10-18653-v1-2024-eacl-demo-16.claim: RAGAs provides automated reference-free metrics for measuring faithfulness and answer relevance in RAG architectures.

doi-10-18653-v1-2020-emnlp-main-550.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
doi-10-18653-v1-2020-emnlp-main-550.support_excerpt: Open-domain question answering relies on efficient passage retrieval to select candidate contexts. We show that retrieval can be practically implemented using dense representations.
doi-10-18653-v1-2020-emnlp-main-550.claim: Dense passage retrieval leverages dual-encoder architectures for semantically grounded context selection.

doi-10-18653-v1-2023-eacl-main-148.title: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
doi-10-18653-v1-2023-eacl-main-148.support_excerpt: Text embeddings are evaluated across 8 embedding tasks and 58 datasets in the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB).
doi-10-18653-v1-2023-eacl-main-148.claim: MTEB provides a holistic benchmark for evaluating text embeddings across diverse retrieval and semantic similarity tasks.

doi-10-18653-v1-2026-findings-eacl-110.title: Which Works Best for Vietnamese? A Practical Study of Information Retrieval Methods across Domains
doi-10-18653-v1-2026-findings-eacl-110.support_excerpt: A comprehensive study comparing lexical, dense, and hybrid information retrieval methods across multiple Vietnamese domains including legal corpora.
doi-10-18653-v1-2026-findings-eacl-110.claim: Vietnamese domain-specific IR benefits from hybrid lexical-dense ranking tailored to linguistic compound structures.

doi-10-18653-v1-2021-naacl-main-200.title: KILT: a Benchmark for Knowledge Intensive Language Tasks
doi-10-18653-v1-2021-naacl-main-200.support_excerpt: KILT benchmarks knowledge-intensive language tasks requiring grounded evidence retrieval.
doi-10-18653-v1-2021-naacl-main-200.claim: Knowledge-intensive tasks require verifiable evidence provenance tied to specific document passages.

doi-10-18653-v1-d19-1410.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
doi-10-18653-v1-d19-1410.support_excerpt: Sentence-BERT (SBERT) modifies pre-trained BERT networks using siamese and triplet structures to derive semantically meaningful sentence embeddings that can be compared using cosine similarity.
doi-10-18653-v1-d19-1410.claim: SBERT produces fixed-size semantic vectors enabling high-throughput cosine similarity retrieval over passage indexes.

doi-10-18653-v1-2025-nllp-1-3.title: Towards Reliable Retrieval in RAG Systems for Large Legal Datasets
doi-10-18653-v1-2025-nllp-1-3.support_excerpt: Investigating document-level retrieval mismatch and reliable passage extraction in legal RAG architectures.
doi-10-18653-v1-2025-nllp-1-3.claim: Legal RAG systems require statutory metadata filtering to prevent cross-statute passage retrieval mismatches.

doi-10-18653-v1-2026-eacl-long-8.title: T2-RAGBench: Text-and-Table Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation
doi-10-18653-v1-2026-eacl-long-8.support_excerpt: Benchmarking retrieval-augmented generation systems on heterogeneous documents containing both unstructured text and tabular data.
doi-10-18653-v1-2026-eacl-long-8.claim: Heterogeneous documents require joint text-and-table representations to preserve structured statutory schedules.

doi-10-18653-v1-2024-nllp-1-14.title: Measuring the Groundedness of Legal Question-Answering Systems
doi-10-18653-v1-2024-nllp-1-14.support_excerpt: Evaluating the groundedness and factual adherence of legal question-answering systems against statutory source documents.
doi-10-18653-v1-2024-nllp-1-14.claim: Groundedness in legal QA requires verifying that generated statutory conclusions strictly derive from cited legal provisions.
